title: The table from heaven
hook: the disciples ask Isa for a table spread from heaven, and he prays for it (5:112–115)

segments.voice: Yesterday: kaffarah, the covering of a broken oath. Your line was swear less. Did a plain yes or no do the job? Today, the scene that gives surah five its name. Day three hundred ninety-six.

Every surah has a name, and most are taken from a word or a scene inside it. Surah five has been called al-Ma'idah for more than a week now, the Table Spread, and so far there hasn't been a table. It arrives near the very end. Isa, Jesus son of Mary, is with his closest followers, the ones the Qur'an calls al-hawariyyun, the disciples. They've seen him heal. They've heard him teach. And they ask him for something that sounds, at first, almost like a dare.
screen: `AL-MA'IDAH — THE TABLE SPREAD.` → `ISA AND THE DISCIPLES.` → `A REQUEST LIKE A DARE.`

segments.voice: Verse one-twelve. The disciples say: O Isa, son of Maryam, is your Lord able to send down for us, in Pickthall's words, “a table spread with food from heaven?” Isa's first answer is a warning: be mindful of Allah, if you truly believe. So they explain themselves, and their reasons are very human. We want to eat from it. We want our hearts to be at rest. We want to know for sure that you've told us the truth. And we want to be witnesses to it. Then Isa prays. He asks Allah to send down a table that will be a feast for them, for the first of them and the last of them, and a sign, and he ends by calling Allah the best of providers. The Arabic word for that feast is 'id, the word in Eid, and this verse is the only place it appears in the Qur'an. Allah answers: I will send it down. But whoever disbelieves after that will face a punishment like no other. A sign that clear raises the stakes for everyone who sees it. Did the table actually come down? The Qur'an gives the promise, but never narrates the table arriving, and never tells us what was on it. Early commentators disagreed. Many said yes, and passed on reports about bread and fish. Others, including the early scholars Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri, said that when the disciples heard the warning, they withdrew the request, and no table came. What the text does keep is the shape of a good table: a need named honestly, a prayer made for the first and the last, and the One who provides.
screen: `IS YOUR LORD ABLE?` · `HEARTS AT REST, AND WITNESSES.` · `'ID — A FEAST, FIRST AND LAST.` · `DID IT COME DOWN? THEY DIFFERED.` · then, large: `A TABLE SPREAD FROM HEAVEN.`

segments.voice: Sit, and breathe. Picture a table you've eaten at that felt like more than food: a holiday, a hospital cafeteria with someone you love, a picnic, a late-night kitchen. Who was there? Who set it? Now picture a table you could set this week for someone else. It can be tiny: a plate of fruit for a roommate, a meal dropped at a door, a chair pulled out for someone who usually eats alone. Hold that picture. The bell holds the time.
Ma'idah, a table spread with food. The table the disciples asked for and Isa prayed for, a feast for the first and the last. Today's word.
Your line: a table sent down. Today, set a table for someone, even a small one, and notice what it means to provide. Day three hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: Muslims know surah five as al-Ma'idah, named for this table; commentators teach the scene as Isa's prayer for provision and as a lesson that clear signs bring greater responsibility.

fork.setup: you're Isa's disciples. Isa warns you to be mindful of Allah after your request. what do you do?
options: explain why you asked: to eat, to have hearts at rest, to be witnesses.
fork.reveal: they explained themselves honestly, and Isa then prayed for the table on their behalf.

original.note: Arabic: a table spread with food. it names surah five, al-Ma'idah.

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle picnic.
what it means: a sign asked for with honest reasons, prayed for by Isa, with a warning that clear signs raise the stakes.
what a scholar hears: 5:114 has the Qur'an's only use of 'id; Ibn Kathir reports both views on whether the table came down, citing Mujahid and al-Hasan for the view that it did not.

sources.quoted: a table spread with food from heaven

sources.ref: Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:112–115 (reports from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri)

notes: Claim that 5:114 is the only occurrence of 'id in the Qur'an: please verify.
Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri as holding that the table did not come down: reported in Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari from memory; confirm.
Isa's prayer in 5:114 is paraphrased, not quoted, and not presented as a prayer for the listener to say.
Ma'idah gloss and the hawariyyun as disciples: confirm.

Audit (y2 second sample): the teach quoted Pickthall 5:112 as 'a table spread from heaven', but Pickthall reads 'a table spread with food from heaven'; the quote and its source entry now use Pickthall's words. Confirm against the 1930 text.
